title: Playing off the melody, not the chords
summary: He needs a melody to improvise on, and says his generation played off melody; chord-based playing came later.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you. Sometimes -- this is another thing -- I don't think I ever said this before. Some people play on chord construction. I don't play on chord construction. I like to have a melody. I like to read the music down, and see what the composer intended for it to be. In order for me to play it, to get a feeling out of it. Now,
You don't know what the song is.
-- the song is. What his idea is of anything.
Once you have a melody there, and I can see this melody and play this melody over, and see his idea, then I can improvise on this melody, to do something with it.
Yeah. Yeah. So you can make a melody on his melody, which belongs to his melody.
But I cannot do it on chord construction.

No. No. Because after all, I mean, that is the point. You made your own melody, when you made "Concerto for Cootie". You know, there were your chord constructions and that was your own melody. And I mean, when you are playing somebody else's song, unless you see what that song itself is, it could be any series of small melodies built on those same chord progressions, couldn't it?

Yeah. Well, Cootie, and I guess in any case, the chords are that much built into you anyway, that -- I mean, all you need to do is hear the melody, read the melody and hear the melody. After that, you don't go around thinking about chords, because you know instinctively what chords --

Yeah. Well, another thing -- I mean, that's -- in those days it wasn't -- it hadn't become the fashion to fit in such an enormous number of runs and notes and to cover so much ground at such fast tempos. Or, not necessarily such fast tempos, but filling it in, you know, playing 16ths, or 32s, you know, whatever. And it was much more the thing, wasn't it, to beautify the thing by creating --
